brief.headline: Energy and tech services lead; earnings season opens with crowded risk-on tape
brief.regime_summary: SPY is +0.75% above its 50DMA and +6.9% above its 200DMA, with a 1-year max drawdown of just -0.77%, confirming a healthy risk-on regime. VIX at 18.4 is elevated versus its 20DMA of 16.3, signaling some caution creeping in beneath the surface. Seven of eleven sectors are below their 50DMAs, so breadth (6 of 11 above) is acceptable but not broad. Sector momentum is led by energy, healthcare and staples, while XLK and XLC are the only sectors printing negative 20-day momentum, a notable split given how much of the index they represent.

portfolio.note: Earnings on Oct 28. Price at $532.95 is 1.5% above the 20DMA ($525.13) with RSI 59 and 20-day momentum +6.5%, a clean setup into the print. ATR is 2.1%, so a one-ATR miss would put price back at the 20DMA; that level is the line to watch post-earnings.

Price sits 4.1% below its 20DMA and 10.5% below its 20-day high, with RSI at 44 and 20-day momentum -3.9%. The earnings revision story remains intact (+7.5% EPS, +3.7% revenue), but the technical setup has deteriorated into mixed-MA territory; the thesis is intact but the tape is not confirming it yet.

Best momentum in the portfolio: 20-day +9.3%, RSI 68, and price just 0.7% from its 20-day high. XLE sector momentum leads all sectors at +9.3%; cost basis at $88 implies an unrealized loss of 22.5%, but the trend is clearly recovering.

GLD at $378.95 is -3.6% from its 20-day high with RSI 43 and 20-day momentum -3.6%, lagging the market by 4.2% over 20 days. Underlying gold futures show similar softness (-4.5% vs 40DMA, RSI 37); in a risk-on tape, the defensive-asset headwind is structural until regime shifts.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: ACN surged 11.8% last week and is now 17.3% above its 20DMA and 40.1% above its 100DMA, a move that pulled RSI to 77. Forward P/E of 15.1 is unusually low for the name, and EPS and revenue revisions are both positive (+5.7% and +5.3%). The ATR of 3.6% means the 20DMA ($204.82) is roughly 10 ATRs away; a pullback toward $225 to $228 would be the first orderly re-test of prior breakout structure. Earnings are not until Dec 17, so there is no near-term catalyst risk.
watchlist.risk: RSI at 77 and vol at 66% annualized mean a sharp mean-reversion is possible on any market-wide risk-off day.

watchlist.name: ServiceNow
watchlist.thesis: NOW printed a 9.4% gain last week and reports earnings Oct 28. Price is 9.7% above its 20DMA ($139.55) with RSI 66 and above-average volume (rel vol 1.22). Forward P/E of 30.6 is 22% below its historical median of 123, which removes a common objection to the name. Revenue growth is guided at 22% for the year.
watchlist.risk: Earnings on Oct 28 could reset the entire move; a miss on billings or guidance would send price back toward the 20DMA quickly.

watchlist.name: ConocoPhillips
watchlist.thesis: COP is up 2.3% this week and 13.7% over 20 days, with RSI 71 and 8.4% above its 20DMA. Volume is running above average (rel vol 1.08). EPS revisions are up 7.0% and energy sector momentum is the strongest in the market. Reports Nov 5.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $134.44 (implied), 20-day high: $147.43 (implied from -1.2% gap), ATR stop distance: ~$3.28 (2.3%)
watchlist.risk: P/E is 46% above historical median; any softening in crude prices would compress both earnings and the multiple simultaneously.

watchlist.name: Shopify
watchlist.thesis: SHOP is 7.3% above its 20DMA with 20-day momentum of +22.5% and a bullish MA stack. RS vs the market is +21.8% over 20 days. EPS estimates are largely flat, but price and earnings growth of 33.6% support the premium. Reports Nov 3.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $162.46 (implied), 20-day high: ~$180.80 (implied from -3.6% gap), ATR stop distance: ~$7.46 (4.3%)
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E of 117.8x leaves no room for a guidance miss into a tape where XLK momentum is already negative.

watchlist.name: Bank of America
watchlist.thesis: BAC is in a full bearish MA stack: -5.0% vs 20DMA, -10.9% vs 40DMA, -13.0% vs 100DMA. RSI is 25, which is deeply oversold, but 15 analysts cut estimates in the past 30 days with zero upgrades, and EPS revisions are -4.8%. The 20-day momentum is -9.3% in a sector (XLF) that itself shows only +2.8% momentum, lagging badly.
watchlist.risk: RSI at 25 makes a technical bounce possible; any positive macro read on rates or credit could trigger a short squeeze.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC fell 5.3% last week and sits 27.1% below its 20-day high. Price is 13.9% below its 20DMA and the stock is losing 24.9% on a 20-day relative basis vs the market. Reports Oct 29, which is the key catalyst event. ATR is 6.0%, the widest in the screen, so moves around earnings will be large.
watchlist.risk: Consensus EPS growth estimate of 264% for the year means any upside surprise could produce a violent short-cover rally.

commodities.name: Brent crude
commodities.note: Brent at $111.79 is up 5.5% this week, near its 20-day high, and printing a bullish MA stack with RSI 68. The move is consistent with broader energy sector leadership; watch $108 (20DMA) as the first support if crude retreats.

commodities.name: WTI crude
commodities.note: WTI at $99.46 is up 1.5% on the week and 5.1% over 20 days, but still 10% below its 20-day high, lagging Brent, which flags a widening Brent-WTI spread worth monitoring.

commodities.name: Gold futures
commodities.note: Gold at $4,105.60 is down 1.6% on the week and 4.5% below its 40DMA with RSI at 37. Risk-on tape is suppressing safe-haven demand; the 20DMA is the level to reclaim for any bullish re-engagement.

commodities.name: Natural gas
commodities.note: Natural gas dropped 15% this week to $2.75, sitting 10.7% below its 20DMA and 17.5% off its 20-day high despite a technically bullish MA stack on longer timeframes. RSI at 36 signals momentum exhaustion to the downside; a stabilization would be worth flagging.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.note: Wheat fell 6.0% this week to 629.75, with RSI at 28.8 (deeply oversold) and 20-day momentum at -10.9%. The oversold read may attract value interest, but the downtrend vs all moving averages is intact.

risks: Earnings cluster: MSFT and NOW both report Oct 28, INTC on Oct 29. A risk-off earnings reaction in any of these large-cap tech names would test the narrow breadth underpinning the current rally.
VIX at 18.4 is 13.1% above its 20DMA of 16.3, suggesting options markets are pricing in near-term uncertainty even as equity prices hold near highs.
XLK 20-day momentum is -3.5%, the worst of any sector, yet technology remains the largest index weight. Continued sector-level underperformance widens the gap between SPY and an equal-weight view.
Brent crude above $111 sustains an inflation re-acceleration risk that could shift Fed tone if sustained into November data prints.
BAC EPS estimates cut by 15 analysts in 30 days with zero upgrades points to deteriorating credit or net-interest-margin expectations in financials, the second-largest sector weight.
